data.name: The Long Road
data.description: A merchant needs an escort for a cart of trade goods on the long road between waystations. The quiet stretches are the dangerous ones.
data.successDescription: Cart delivered whole. The merchant pays gladly.

objectives.description:
The merchant checks the cart straps for the third time.

"It's one long road and two quiet stretches, they say.
The quiet is what worries me.
Walk with the cart and keep your hands free."
Escort the cart along the first stretch of the long road.

The second stretch.
Birdsong stops.
A lone figure steps out of the treeline ahead of the cart, weapon already drawn.
The merchant goes very pale behind you.
Drive off the ambusher and protect the cart.
objectives.drawDescription: Neither side yielded. The contract stands.
objectives.failDescription: They were stronger than the posting suggested. Regroup.

objectives.description: The ambusher forced you back and the merchant fled to the last waystation with the cart. Regroup and walk the road again.
The ambusher limps into the trees and the cart rolls into the waystation whole. The merchant counts out your pay twice, to be sure.

data.name: The Tenth Name
data.description: A page taken off a body lists ten entries. Nine are copied out of our own Bingo Book in a hand that is not ours. The tenth has no name on it, only a service number with this village's prefix and a date eight months out. Copies are in transit.
data.successDescription: Nobody infiltrated anything. The four fields on every entry are public record, printed by this village about its own people and pinned to a wall.

objectives.description: A rank. Retrieval. The briefing room, and a single page on the table, folded twice.

Ten entries.

"Nine of them I recognise, because nine of them are entries out of our own Bingo Book, copied in a hand that is not ours."

"They keep a book on themselves. On its own that is a week's work."

The tenth line has no name on it. A service number, a village prefix, and a date eight months out.

The prefix is ours.

"Currently serving, with a date on them like a delivery."

She does not look the number up in front of you.

nextObjectiveId.text: What do you want me to bring back?

objectives.description:
"This page is stock. Copies are moving between their people right now, and every hour it circulates it goes somewhere I cannot follow."

"Take one out of transit and bring me the route it was on. Page and route. Not the person."

Three places a copy might be moving through, and one of them is a cold room.
You walk the canal frontage looking for a stone with two strokes on it.

Four stones, four single strokes, none of them fresh.

The lanes here were worked last week and have not been booked since. Whatever is moving is not moving through this frontage tonight.
The gate ledgers go back a month and every line of them is somebody's name.

Nobody carrying that page walked through a gate and signed for it.

An afternoon proving that people who deal in unsigned paper also do not sign for themselves.
The body it came off is still in the cold room, unidentified, which is the normal outcome and not a failure. You go through the coat seam by seam.

No plate, no papers. In the coat lining, a chalk stub worn to the length of a thumbnail.

The page was carried folded twice against the body, the way you carry something you refer to often.

Working stock, not a delivery. Which means a route, and a route means a runner.
Three ways to take a copy out of transit, and only one night to do it.

nextObjectiveId.text: Stand in the lane at the hour and take it.
Follow a runner instead of stopping one.

objectives.description: You take the third street of the frontage, where the stone has two strokes and the second is still powdery, and you give it the hour.

Two come down the lane at the hour the chalk gives. They stop when they see somebody standing in it.

There is a pause in which one of them clearly considers explaining that you are in the wrong place, and then decides against it.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
The lane empties in both directions and takes the hour with it.

In the morning the stone has been scrubbed and there are three fresh strokes on a corner two streets over.
You pick up a runner at the frontage and stay with them for four streets without closing, which is harder than closing.
You stay with the chain for two hours and write down every stone it touches.

Four handovers in two hours, none of them the same person twice, every one at a corner stone.

Nobody passes a page. They pass a place.

The route runs inward from the canal and ends at a reading room off the records annexe.

nextObjectiveId.text: Take the last one in the chain.

objectives.description: The last runner in the chain is standing in the annexe doorway with a copy in their hand and no idea that the four ahead of them are already accounted for.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
They are through the annexe door and into the boards room before you are past the step, and out the other side into a street full of people.

The chain will not run that route again this week.
You spend the evening in the wrong sort of room asking what a copy of a page would cost.

It costs about what a good meal costs, which is the single most useful thing you learn all night.

The man who sells it has never read it, cannot read most of it, and does not care. He copies what he is given and sells the copies on.

"They are not secret," he says, honestly baffled by the question. "They are just not for you."

nextObjectiveId.text: Buy one and ask where his came from.

objectives.description: He tells you, and then the two men whose route you have just bought your way into come through the door behind you.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description: You go out of the window and the room is empty behind you, and by morning nobody in that quarter is selling anything to anybody.

The nine known entries all carry the same three fields under the name. A year, a prefix, and a single word.

Passed. Debt. Discipline. Passed. Clanless. Debt. Discipline. Passed. Debt.
You take the reading room itself and go through what is pinned up in it.

Promotion boards go up on a wall four times a year. The lending register is open to any creditor who asks. Discipline dockets are posted so the punishment is seen to be done.

Nobody infiltrated anything.

This village publishes a list of the people it has disappointed, on purpose, and somebody has been walking in and reading it.

She reads the four fields before she reads the tenth line.

"Every one of these is on a wall somewhere in this village with my authority at the bottom of it."

"They are not recruiting out of our ranks. They are standing at the bottom of a slope we built and pointed downhill."

nextObjectiveId.text: Eight months is a forecast, not a plan.
The tenth has not done anything.

objectives.description:
"A forecast that will probably be right, which is worse. Nobody has spoken to this person. Nobody has offered them anything."

"Somebody read four public facts and wrote a date, and on the evidence of the nine above it I would not bet against the date."

nextObjectiveId.text: So what happens to the page?

objectives.description:
"Nothing at all. Which is the problem I am about to have upstairs, because the moment this goes up, everybody matching those four fields becomes a watch list."

"And then the date will be right for reasons we caused."

nextObjectiveId.text: So what happens to the page?

objectives.description:
She has the page and the route, which is what she asked for. What happens next is not a field decision, and she says so, and then asks anyway.

"You walked that route. Tell me what you think and then I will ignore you if I want to."

nextObjectiveId.text: Put the page up and let us read it too.

objectives.description:
Somebody knocks. Not you, and not that week.

It comes back as a line in a personnel note. The officer was spoken to, was cooperative, and has requested no further contact.

"Cooperative," she reads out, with no expression at all.

"They now know they were on a list. The date is still eight months away and I have made it more likely, not less."

She files the page.

"The page was worth taking. What we do with it is a different problem and it is mine."

Nobody knocks. The service number is never looked up.

What goes upstairs is a proposal about the reading room, and it takes seven months and most of her remaining goodwill.

It removes exactly one of the four fields.

"One of four means the next list is harder to build and less accurate. It is also the only one of the four that cost this village nothing to give up, which is why it is the one I got."

"Be angrier about that than I am able to be in this office."

The page goes up with your report and the route drawn out in full.

It comes back in nine days approved for circulation to section heads. Everybody matching those four fields is now a name on a desk somewhere.

"They wanted it read. Now it is read by us as well, and I cannot decide whether that is counter-intelligence or doing their filing."

She signs the circulation.

"Nine of those section heads will treat it as a warning about the village. One will treat it as a list of suspects. I do not get to choose which."
Page recovered.
The frontage, and the chain of runners.
The page, and what is on it.

data.name: The Empty Contract
data.description: A dead courier was carrying a strange contract. It names a place, a night, and a price, but it does not say what the job is. The price is far too high for a simple beating. The night is tonight.
data.successDescription: Nobody was planning a robbery. Someone was paid to time the patrols, and that number will sell to anybody.

objectives.description:
The handler has a paper under a stone and a mission slip clipped to it.

The slip reads: C rank. The paper was taken off a courier found dead on the north road. It looked like an accident. There was nothing else on the body.

nextObjectiveId.text: Just tell me where to be.

objectives.description:
Four lines. A place. A night. A price. Instead of a signature, only a drawn mark.

There is no instruction of any kind. And the price is enough money to live on for a season.

nextObjectiveId.text: Too much money for a simple job.

objectives.description:
That much money does not buy a beating. It buys something else.

And the paper never says what. A place, a night, a price, and no task written anywhere on it.

Which is the point. A contract that names the job can only be carried by somebody allowed to know the job. This one can be dropped in a road.

The place is the roof of a disused dyer's shop on the tannery row. The building is empty. The yard behind it is empty. Nothing there is worth stealing.

So the roof itself is not the prize. The prize is what you can see from the roof.

nextObjectiveId.text: Go and look at what the roof can see.

objectives.description:
The dyer's shop is four storeys of empty building on a corner nobody uses.

The roof looks straight down onto the north watch post, and onto both streets the night patrol uses.

Someone is lying flat at the roof edge, chin on their arms. They have been up there for hours. Every few minutes they scratch a mark into a wax tablet without taking their eyes off the street.

nextObjectiveId.text: Climb the back wall. Slow, but silent.
Take the stairs. Fast, but loud.
Wait at the bottom door. They must come down.

objectives.description: The back wall is brick under forty years of ivy. Climbing it quietly takes a long time. Quiet is the whole point.

You come over the roof edge eight feet behind them. They do not hear you.

The tablet lies open beside their elbow, and they are still writing. Four hours of marks, and every mark is neat and steady.
You wait by the alley door at the bottom of the stairs. Everyone has to come down eventually.

They come down four hours later, at the end of their shift, and walk straight past you. To them, you are just someone waiting in a doorway.

The tablet is inside their coat.
They only notice the danger when you are four feet away. They grab for the tablet, not for a weapon.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
They get over the far wall with the tablet and are gone into the tannery row.

But the contract pays for a full night of times, and half a tablet is worth nothing. Before long, a figure climbs back onto the roof and settles in again.

nextObjectiveId.text: Go back to the dyer's roof.

objectives.description:
The stair door is stiff, and it screeches loud enough to warn the whole building. By the time you reach the roof, they are already two roofs away with the tablet under one arm.

You chase them over four roofs, a yard wall, and half the tannery row.
You corner them in a dead end above the drying sheds. Even now, they try to slip past you instead of fighting you.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
They jump off the drying shed roof into the dark and take the tablet with them.

But the contract pays for a full night of times, and half a tablet is worth nothing. Before long, they are back at the roof edge, writing again.

nextObjectiveId.text: Go back to the dyer's roof.

objectives.description:
The watcher sits against the wall, beaten, and says nothing. They watch you read.

Four hours of times and nothing else. Two columns, one for each patrol street. A mark every time the patrol comes out. A mark every time it goes back in.

At the bottom, underlined twice, a single number: eleven.

nextObjectiveId.text: Take the tablet back to the hall.

objectives.description:
At the hall, the handler reads halfway down the second column and goes quiet. He reads it again from the top.

"Look at the handwriting. Steady all the way through. Four hours of marks, and it never shook once."

"A thief planning his own robbery would be nervous. This is a copyist's hand. Someone paid to write down times, and never told them what the times were for."

"And here is what they proved. Twice a night, for eleven minutes, nobody is watching the north post. That gap is the product. A number like that will sell to anybody."

He puts the tablet down on top of the contract.

"The courier was not killed, by the way. He came off a wet road in the dark and broke his neck on it. Nobody arranged that."

"Everything these people build is designed so that no one person knows enough to give the rest away. It works. And then it rains."

nextObjectiveId.text: Eleven minutes, and a number that sells.

objectives.description: Contract logged, watcher taken.
The dyer's roof, and the streets the patrol uses.

data.name: The Waystation
data.description: The keeper of the pass waystation is going home to open it again. The posting says: guard her from bandits, two days up the pass road. The pay is low, even for C rank.
data.successDescription: The posting said bandits. It was never bandits.

objectives.description:
A posting on the board: an escort, two days up the pass road. Guard the client from bandits.

The slip reads: C rank. One traveler. The pay is low, even for C rank.

The client is the keeper of the waystation at the top of the pass. She ran it for thirty years, and now she is going back up to open it again.

The handler has added a note by hand: she asked twice whether an escort is released if a job turns out worse than its posting. She asked it like someone who already knew the answer.

The keeper waits at the village gate with a pack of tools, no valuables, and a straight back. She sets off without being told, and she does not look behind her once.

The low road runs past the toll shed toward the foot of the pass.

nextObjectiveId.text: Ask at the toll shed first.

objectives.description:
You stop at the toll shed and let the toll man talk. He talks about bandit trouble easily, at length, and a little too readily.

In the whole conversation, he never once asks who you are guarding.

Where the road narrows, you read the ground. A fire pit, two days cold. Cut stems at boot height on both sides of the track. A flat stone worn smooth where a man sat for hours, facing downhill, toward the village.

Bandits watch a road for whoever comes along it. These men were waiting for someone.

They come out of the cut brush on both sides at once. Rags over their mouths, no plates on their foreheads.

They fight like men paid by the day. The moment it turns, the paid day is over.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
Two sides at once is one side too many, and they know this ground.

They pull back down the slope and re-form where the road narrows. They are paid to hold this stretch, so they will be standing in it again.

Bandits rob whoever the road brings them. These men were placed on the one road one woman has to take, days before she took it.

And a shut waystation still has a road under it. Somebody has spent a year standing on that road taking what the station used to take, and writing none of it down. An open door at the top of the pass ends that on the first morning.

The posting said bandits. The posting was wrong. And the rule on every slip is plain: a false posting frees the escort. You may turn back now, paid for the road you walked, with no fault written against you.

The keeper has not stopped walking.

"I wrote bandits. Bandits is what I could afford."

nextObjectiveId.text: Turn back. The posting was false.

objectives.description:
Above the ambush ground the way splits.

The pass road climbs wide and open, in view of the ridge the whole way. The old stair cut goes straight up through the rocks: steep, narrow, and out of sight.

nextObjectiveId.text: Take the pass road, and watch the ridge.

objectives.description:
You put the keeper behind a boulder and watch the ridge line.

A shape against the sky holds still for a long time. Then it gives up waiting, and moves to where the pass narrows.

Two of them at the neck of the pass. The younger one stands the way the first two stood.

The other one holds his ground like a man who was trained once, and remembers most of it.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
The stair cut is four hundred steps of broken stone with grass growing through them.

You climb with the keeper's hand on your shoulder, and you come out above the pass, behind everything that is watching it.

One man sits at the top of the stair with his back against the waystation wall, out of the wind.

He was paid to make sure nobody reached this door. Nobody told him about the stair. Now he has to earn the money, and he does not like it.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
The high ground wins, and the pass throws you back down to the fork.

The keeper waits there with her pack still on. She does not say anything. She simply waits to go up again.

The waystation door has been shut for a year, and it opens on the first pull.

The keeper walks the rooms once, opens the shutters, and lays a fire in the cold hearth like she never left.

When you reach the first bend of the road down, there is already smoke standing up from the chimney behind you.

You bring the keeper back down and set the slip on the desk with the release written under it.

The handler reads it, signs it off without comment, and pays out the road you walked.

She goes back up the pass alone the next morning. You are not told how it ends.

nextObjectiveId.text: The posting was false. Release taken.

objectives.description:
The handler reads the report twice. The false posting. The prepared ground. A year of tolls collected at an empty station.

"A false posting frees the escort. You knew that, and you finished the road anyway."

"That is worth knowing about a person. And someone will be walking up to ask about those tolls."
Road walked, station open.
The road narrows, and the ground still reads the same.
The fork below the pass.

objectives.description:
The clerk speaks without looking up, very quietly.

"A week of postings went to the wrong boards. If you collect the misplaced ones and repin them on the correct ones."
"This conversation never happened."
Collect the misplaced postings from around the village.
Repin the postings at the annex board.

data.name: Copies, Not Thefts
data.description: Three of the Kage's letters were copied, not stolen. Get inside a private archive, take back the files, and bring home the ledger that names the buyer. How quietly you do it is up to you.
data.successDescription: Congratulations! You've successfully won the battle

objectives.description:
The briefing room is lit by one lantern over the map table. The Commander does not sit.

"Three of the Kage's letters left this village and came back as copies. Copies, not thefts. Someone wanted us blind, not angry.
The paper traces to a private archive that keeps records for anyone who pays."

nextObjectiveId.text: Why is ANBU not handling this openly?

objectives.description:
She sets a marker on the map, well outside the wall.

"That is what you will find out. Bring back what they hold and the ledger that says who paid. Nobody knows you were there.
One detail, since you will be reading their shelves: that archive files by season, not by year. Anyone who asks for a year has never been inside."

nextObjectiveId.text: And if the door is watched?

objectives.description:
The mission clerk has your kit ready before you reach the counter.

"Lockpicks, ink kit, two smoke tags, and a writ that will not survive a careful reader.
Sign here. Not with your real name, obviously."
Cross to the archive district under dark.

The safehouse smells of cold tea. Through the shutter slat you can see the archive door across the alley.

Two guards, one circuit, four minutes apart. There will be a service way in around the back, and a roof line if you would rather be quick than careful.
Work the alley behind the archive and map the ways in.

Three ways in, and the patrol turns in ninety seconds.

The coal chute is filthy, blind and slow. The roof line is quick and completely exposed. The front door would take the writ and a steady face.

nextObjectiveId.text: Take the coal chute. Slow and unseen.
Go over the roof line. Fast and loud.

objectives.description: Crawl the coal chute, one shoulder at a time, and drop into the cellar.

You come out under the stacks with soot in your teeth and nobody the wiser.

Above you the building is quiet in the way that means everyone in it believes they are alone.

The tiles are wet and one of them moves under your foot.

Across the roof a lookout turns, sees you, and does not shout. He reaches for the bell rope instead, which is worse.
Take the lookout down before he reaches the rope.
objectives.drawDescription: Neither side yielded. The contract stands.
objectives.failDescription: They were stronger than the posting suggested. Regroup.

objectives.description:
He does not reach it. But he got a hand to it, and somewhere below a small bell moved once.

One ring is not an alarm. It is a question. Someone in this building is already walking toward the answer.

nextObjectiveId.text: Get inside before they find it.

objectives.description:
The clerk reads the writ twice, which is once more than you wanted.

"Requisition, then. Which index do you need pulled?"

nextObjectiveId.text: The index for the year, all of it.
Whichever one the Kage's office uses.

objectives.description:
He nods, bored, and writes it down. Everyone who works here knows they file by season. Only outsiders ask for a year.

"Third aisle, and do not take the lamp past the ledgers."
He goes back to his tea. You walk into the archive through the front door like a man with business here.

He smiles, and the smile does not reach anything.

"We do not index by year. Never have."

objectives.description:

The name beside them is one you have heard in a briefing room, on the other side of the table.

objectives.description: Work the seal on the file drawer.

Someone has been in the room the whole time.

"You were not seen. Good.

data.name: Witness Detail
data.description: An hour before dawn a witness has to reach a hearing on the other side of the village, and the people who want her absent were paid to take her alive. Three ways across. All of them end in a fight.
data.successDescription: She reached the steps and she gave the name.

objectives.description:
The handler does not sit down, and does not offer you tea. She lays a folded contract on the table and turns it so the price faces you.

"Somebody bought her. Not her death, her absence. Take, was the word they used."

nextObjectiveId.text: Absence buys silence. Death buys questions.

objectives.description:
She does not agree out loud. She taps the table twice with one finger, the way you tap a wall in the dark to find the door.

"The last one I sent asked me why they had not simply killed her. Since you are quicker than him, keep up. The Unsigned chalk a lane before they work it, one stroke, low on the corner stone. Not a warning to you. A note they leave each other."

nextObjectiveId.text: Then I will read their notes.

objectives.description:
She looks up properly for the first time, and does not quite hide that she is reassessing you.

"Slowly, then. A body is a crime. Somebody has to investigate a crime, and investigating this one means reading the ledger she was going to talk about. A witness who simply fails to arrive is nobody's case at all. Now, the Unsigned chalk a lane before they work it. One stroke, low on the corner stone. It is not a warning meant for you, it is a note they leave each other."

nextObjectiveId.text: Then I will read their notes.

objectives.description:
Kanna is twenty two, has not slept, and holds a rolled statement against her chest like it is the only warm thing she owns.

"They came to my father's house first," she says. "They were very polite about it. That is the part I keep thinking about."

She is at the door with her coat already on, standing at your left shoulder like she was told. Past it the village is dark for another hour, and somewhere in that hour people are standing very still, waiting to be told which way the two of you went.

"You choose," she says. "I have been choosing all week and look where it put me."

nextObjectiveId.text: The market road. Loud rooms hide loud men.
The back lanes. Slow, blind, ours.
Give me your coat. You walk alone.

objectives.description: The market road is loud with carts before dawn, which is cover of a kind, and a hundred witnesses, which is not.

A fruit seller looks at you twice and then does not look at all. Two men come through the crowd at walking pace, because hurrying is what a crowd remembers.

"The polite one is on the left," Kanna says. Her voice does not shake, which is somehow worse.
Two of them working the crowd. Neither one looks at Kanna, which means each is counting on the other to reach her first.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent
objectives.successDescription: The crowd closes over it before it has finished happening. She has not moved from behind your shoulder.

objectives.description: The back lanes take three times as long and cross no open ground at all. A patrol passes the lane mouth and you wait it out with her hand over her own mouth.

Chalk on the corner stone. One stroke, low down, unweathered. The rain stopped two hours ago.

"It is only chalk," Kanna whispers. "Children do that."

nextObjectiveId.text: Children do not chalk at midnight. Take the parallel.

objectives.description:
You take the parallel and leave theirs empty. Somewhere behind you a lane that somebody spent the evening preparing stays quiet all the way to dawn, and nobody standing in it ever learns why.

"Children," Kanna says, eventually. "Yes. That was stupid of me."
Not children. The lane was chalked because it is long, and blind, and opens at one end, and what is waiting at that end has been waiting a while.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent
objectives.successDescription: You get out of the lane. It costs you.

objectives.description:
The coat is tight across your shoulders and smells of her house. She takes the servants' stair without being told twice.

"If they take you instead of me," she says from the dark, "I am still going. I wanted you to know that first."
They send the good one after the coat. She works out that it is empty about four steps too late, and does not stop, because she was not paid to stop.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent
objectives.successDescription: The coat is ruined. Kanna is three streets away and has not been touched.

objectives.description: The hearing hall stands at the top of eleven steps. The bell has not rung.

Someone has been sitting on the steps long enough that the frost has taken the shape of him. He stands at the exact distance where leaving stops being something you can do quietly.

"She has an hour," he says. "I only need her to miss it."

nextObjectiveId.text: Then you come through me first.

objectives.description: He takes you up on it without a word. No lane, no crowd, no coat. Eleven steps, and a bell about to ring.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent
objectives.successDescription: The bell rings on the second stroke of it. She walks up past you and does not look down.

objectives.description:
The clerk checks the hour before he checks her name, and writes them down in that order.

"If she had come in after the bell," he says, still writing, "I would have noted that instead, and there would be nothing here to hear. No crime in it. The record does not ask why a person was late."

nextObjectiveId.text: One hour. That was the whole price of her.

objectives.description: Witness delivered, statement taken.

You come to in a doorway with your collar gone stiff. Two doors down, behind the water butt, something that has been holding still for twenty minutes moves.

"I did what you told me," Kanna says. "The bell has not rung yet. Get up."
The safehouse, the lamp oil, the three ways across the village.

data.name: Three Rounds
data.description: A four person squad went to watch a bonded handover on the east road and has missed two signal windows. Four B rank shinobi have gone quiet inside our own border.
data.successDescription: He was never unbeatable. He was expensive, and he could not afford himself for longer than a minute.

objectives.description:
There is no slip for this one on the open board. It is pinned on the wall behind the desk, and somebody comes and finds you before you have finished reading it.

A rank. Search and rescue.

A squad of four, B rank, sent to watch a bonded handover on the east road. Observation only.

Eleven hours overdue. Two signal windows missed.

nextObjectiveId.text: Read the rest of the file.

objectives.description:
Four names, four service records, and a note in the margin of the tasking, in somebody else's hand: observation only, do not engage under any circumstances.

Somebody expected this handover to be dangerous, and sent four people to look at it anyway.

The ridge track runs above the east road for the last mile of it.

nextObjectiveId.text: Take the ridge and come down onto it from above.

objectives.description: The ridge sits forty feet above the road. You come down onto the site from it, slowly, reading the ground on the way in.

Three of them, in a rough diamond, none more than five paces from the next.

Two were put down by a single strike each. The third took two, and the second was not necessary. Not one of them raised an arm.

Four sets of prints arrive together and stop. They never spread out. They never fell back. And nothing left down the road.

nextObjectiveId.text: Four went out. Three are here.

objectives.description:
A fifth set of prints comes out of the treeline, crosses to the diamond, and goes back the way it came.

Same stride in as out. Nobody walks back from this at the pace they walked in at.

The fourth of the squad did not go down the road, and they did not go into the trees.
You work the rock line above the site outward, one section at a time.

Half a mile along it, wedged under an overhang with burns down one side, is the fourth.

Awake. Not walking out on his own.

"I already told nobody I did not see anything."

nextObjectiveId.text: Splint the arm and let him talk when he wants to.

objectives.description:
It comes in pieces, angrily, in the wrong order.

"There was no noise. Kaeda went down and I did not hear her go down."

He stops. Then goes on, because he has started.

"I was behind the rock line already. Not hiding. Already there. I want that written down."

You splint the arm, get water into him, and ask nothing at all.

It takes a while. When it comes, it comes in order.

"It was over before I understood it had started. I have spent eleven hours up here looking for the moment I could have come out."

There is not one. You are fairly sure there is not one.

He answers immediately, which means he has counted it many times.

"Three. Three rounds."

Quieter.

"Then nothing. He stood in the middle of them a while, and walked back to the trees. He was not hurrying. He was breathing like a man who had just run a long way."

You get him onto a horse and down to the relay post, and he talks the whole way. Two others met the man at the treeline afterwards, and neither of them had come from the road. A perimeter, and one person inside it.

She reads the field report at the post rather than waiting for you to come in.

"Three rounds, and then a man getting his breath back. He is not unbeatable. He is expensive, and he cannot afford himself for long."

"And he is still here. Nine days, inside our border, with people standing watch for him. A man who had finished a job would have been over the line the same night."

"So that handover was not one afternoon. He is screening a route, and a route runs until somebody stops it. There is another crossing coming and he intends to be standing over it."

"Pursuit from here. Same rank, different job. Find where he sleeps."
Three places worth an afternoon, and only so many afternoons.

nextObjectiveId.text: The treeline he came out of.
The handover he was sent to interrupt.

objectives.description: The relay post has heard everything and confirmed nothing. You sit in the yard and let the riders talk.

Four riders, four versions, and one of them has him seven feet tall.

Nobody here has been within a mile of the east road.
The handover site is a wide place on the old cut, where two carts can pass. You walk it end to end.

The handover happened. Cart ruts, a scuff of boots, and nothing else at all.

It went off without a single incident. Now you know why. He was not sent to interrupt it. He was sent to make sure nobody watched it, and by the time the carts met, nobody was.

The treeline is where he came from and where he went back to, and the two who met him there did not come from the road.

Three ways to work it, and they do not lead to the same place.

nextObjectiveId.text: Put a collection on the board and wait at the stone.
Follow the two who met him instead.

objectives.description: The trail runs north out of the thorn, and stops being a trail about a mile in.
It does not stop because he hid it. It stops because somebody tidied it. And tidied is worse than hidden. Hidden is one man being careful. Tidied is somebody doing the careful part for him.

Three come out of the field line at once, spread wide, and none of them closes.

They are not trying to beat you. They are trying to keep you standing in this field.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
They hold you exactly as long as they meant to, and then leave in three directions.

The north road is empty, and whatever it was covering has had its head start.

Every crew in this district books its ground the same way: a stroke on a corner stone, and a figure under it. You chalk a heavy figure with a date six days out, then take the doorway across the street and give it the evening.

It is read a little after dark.

Not taken. Read. Somebody stood at that stone long enough to learn the figure, and walked away without touching it.
They come back to the stone an hour later to check it a second time. It is the only mistake anybody has made all week.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
They are over the wall before you are up.

By morning, the stroke has been scrubbed off the stone with a wet hand.
The two who met him at the treeline went south on foot, and they are not more than a day ahead.

You run them down at the edge of the old cut, and they do the last thing you expect. They stop.

Neither is armed. Neither is going to fight you. They are couriers, paid for a walk to a treeline, and they have been paid for that walk four times this month.

They give up the rest without being asked twice. South, off the old cut, there is a drying shed. They never pass its gate. They leave what they carry outside it, and by morning it is gone.

One of them stays on the ground, and you keep him there.

"South. A drying shed off the old cut. He sleeps behind a gate nobody passes. That is every word I have that is not a name."

A place is cheap. A name is fatal. He has given you the only thing his silence sells.

South. A grain drying shed off the old cut. Road on one side, open ground on the other three. Nobody screens a drying shed.

"Then you have him."

She says the rest slowly, because it is the part that matters.

"Three rounds. Spend them trying to win, and you lose in the second, the way four people already have. Spend them staying alive. Then he is a tired man in a shed."

The shed sits an hour south on the old cut.

Tonight, in the dark, through his screen. Or first light, when the screen may not be there at all.
You take the old cut in the dark, and the open ground on three sides turns out to be open in both directions.

Three standing off the shed at intervals, and a fourth shape in the doorway that does not move when the others do.

He is not asleep. He has been awake for the hour you chose.
You lie up in the ditch line and give it the last of the dark.

An hour before the light, the three shapes around the shed detach one by one and walk north.

Nobody gives an order. They go at the hour they always go, because nobody thought to tell them otherwise.

The shed has one person in it, and the road is empty in both directions.

nextObjectiveId.text: Wait for him to come out.

objectives.description:
He comes through his own screen rather than around it, and the three close in behind him, to make sure the ground behind you is theirs.

The first exchange is faster than anything the survivor described. And there are three more people in it than there were on the east road.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent
objectives.successDescription: You are standing at the end of the third round. He is not.

objectives.description:
Four of them, and the second round arrives before you have finished the first.

You get clear of the cut with the shed lit behind you and nobody following. Nobody needs to follow. He won.

nextObjectiveId.text: Come back at a better hour.

objectives.description:
He comes out at first light, because it is the hour he always comes out, and he is halfway to the road before he sees the ditch line.

He does not call for anyone. There is nobody to call. He rolls his shoulder once.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent
objectives.successDescription: You are standing at the end of the third round. He is not.

objectives.description:
You spend the first round trying to win it, and there is no second round for you.

When you come round, he has gone back inside and the door is shut. The shed keeps its one tenant. As far as he knows, nothing that matters has happened.

nextObjectiveId.text: Come back at a better hour.

objectives.description:
"Who told you."

Not a demand. He is working it out, and he is too tired to hide that he is.

nextObjectiveId.text: A man behind a rock line who counted.

objectives.description:
You tell him about the rock line, and about eleven hours of somebody looking for the moment he could have come out.

He listens to all of it.

"Then he was the only one of them who did the right thing. Tell him that. He will not believe it from me."

nextObjectiveId.text: What happens now is not up to you.

objectives.description:
You do not answer, and he does not ask again.

He looks at the light on the road for a while, and laughs once, at nothing you can see.

"Hours. We are very good at hours."

nextObjectiveId.text: What happens now is not up to you.

objectives.description:
He is not being carried anywhere, and both of you know it.

He has a name that three service files do not, and somewhere, a village that trained him.

He goes in without resisting and does not say another word to anyone. Not defiance. He has nothing to add.

"He will not talk. There is nothing he could say that would not be a name."

Then, differently.

"But he is in a cell. And the survivor gets told that the thing which did it is sitting in a building. That is not evidence. It is still worth something."

"Go and tell him he did the right thing. He will not believe it from me either."

nextObjectiveId.text: Three files closed, and a man in a cell.

objectives.description:
Quick, on a road at first light, with nobody watching.

Afterwards there is a man with no name, no plate, and a featureless black mask that three villages could not put a face under. Nothing on him but a chalk stub worn to the length of a thumbnail.

"Three files closed, and a chalk stub. That is the whole estate."

She does not say whether it was the right call. You notice that she does not.

"Go and tell the survivor. Whatever else you tell him, tell him he did the right thing."

nextObjectiveId.text: Three files closed, and a chalk stub.

objectives.description: Squad recovered, target taken.
Three places worth an afternoon.
The treeline, and three ways to work it.
The old cut, and the shed an hour south.

data.successDescription: Every lamp lit. The village glows.

objectives.description:
The note pinned at the board is short and slightly desperate.

"Bad knee.
Oil flask is by the west row.
Lamps in order: west row, then the gate."
"Do not skip the gate, people trip."
Walk to the west lamp row as dusk settles.
Pick up the lamplighter's oil flask.
Finish the rounds at the gate lamps.
The last gate lamp catches and holds. Somewhere, a bad knee rests easier.

data.name: The Loud Way
data.description: Eleven crates signed into a bonded warehouse in four months and never signed out. Nobody reports a theft, and nobody pays four months of bond fees on goods they never touch. Get inside, learn what the building is for, get out.
data.successDescription: The warehouse was never storing anything. It is a place where two people who refuse to meet can hand something over without ever being in the room at the same time.

objectives.description:
B rank on the board. Infiltration, a bonded warehouse on the canal.

You take it to the desk, and the handler sends you upstairs instead. Jobs that go upstairs are not ordinary jobs.

A small room, two ledgers open side by side, and an officer who does not introduce herself.

"Eleven crates in four months. Signed into the bonded yard, never signed out. Nobody has reported a theft. And nobody pays four months of bond fees on goods they never touch."

"Get in, learn what the building is for, get out. B rank, because the people on that yard at night are not amateurs."

nextObjectiveId.text: I will find my own way in.

objectives.description:
Three ways in, and she recommends none of them.

The roofline carries a lookout on the canal side who does not leave when the shift does. The street door is lit, with two men on it on the nights crates move. The canal drain comes up inside the building, and costs an hour on your hands and knees.

"One more thing. The yard hired extra men for tonight. Whatever this building is for, tonight it is for something."
Four ways at it. The night is not getting longer.
The customs office keeps the bond book, and will show it to anyone with a tasking.

Every one of the eleven is signed, sealed, and lawful. The paperwork is perfect.

You have spent an hour learning that the paper will tell you nothing. Whatever is wrong in that building, it is not written down.
The roofline runs unbroken from the barrel maker's to the warehouse gable. You take it slowly, because the lookout is sitting on the far end of it.

They come off the chimney fast and light, and they do not shout. Shouting would tell the whole canal that the roof was watched.

This one intends to leave quietly, and would rather go over you than past you.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
They break over the gable and are three streets gone before you are upright.

Below, the street door stays lit and nobody comes out of it. Whatever they saw, they have not told anyone yet.

Two in identical blank half masks, standing in the light, watching you cross the whole width of the street without once looking at each other.

Neither moves until you are inside arm's reach. Then both move at once.

They are not fast, and they are not trying to be. The doorway is eight feet wide, and they intend to still be standing in it when this finishes.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
Eight feet of doorway, and two people who will not step out of it.

They do not follow you when you go. That is the part that stays with you.

You are on the loading floor inside a minute, which is faster than either of the other ways in.

Every window on the canal now knows the warehouse had something worth guarding. The floor is stacked four high with bonded crates, and every seal on them is unbroken.

nextObjectiveId.text: Work the stacks by seal date.

objectives.description: The canal drain runs under the loading floor and comes up inside the building. An hour on your hands and knees, in water that has been standing since spring.

You come up through the hatch with your boots full of canal, and nobody has heard a thing.

Beside the nearest stack there is a ring in the dust where a man knelt, and the knee print is still damp from the canal fog.

Someone was in here while you were in the water.

The floor is stacked four high with bonded crates, and every seal on them is unbroken.

The building is a quarter full. The eleven are not hidden. They are standing in the open with all the rest.

nextObjectiveId.text: Work the stacks by seal date.

objectives.description: The eleven are not together and not in sequence. Finding what they have in common takes most of an hour.

Every one of them has been opened and resealed. The seals are genuine.

The crates are empty.

A man walks in with a thing and puts it in a crate. He leaves. Days later, a different man opens the crate and takes the thing out. The two are never in the building at the same time, and neither one can name a person he has never met.

Beside the eleventh crate there is a manifest sheet, lying face down, belonging to no crate at all.

Eleven collection times, written in one steady, unhurried hand.

The last time on the sheet is tonight.

nextObjectiveId.text: Put the sheet back and get up in the rafters.

objectives.description: You fold the sheet into your coat and go for the canal door.

Nine steps from it, the street door opens behind you, and does not close.

Nobody says anything. That is worse than if they had.
You go up the stacks into the roof space, settle where the floor cannot see you, and give it the rest of the night.

The canal door opens without a sound.

One person, alone, walking straight to the eleventh crate without looking at anything else in the building. They crouch to read the manifest, and they do not pick it up.

They have not made a noise since the door, and they are not going to.

Three of them, fanning out across the floor without a word. They were not sent to collect a crate. They were sent to make sure the collection was not interrupted.

They can see the corner of the sheet in your coat from where they are standing.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
Three across an open floor is too many, and they know it.

One of them takes the sheet off you, walks it back to the eleventh crate, and lays it down face down, exactly where it was. Then all three step back into the dark of the stacks and wait.

They were paid for the whole night. So were you.
They know you are in the roof before your feet leave it.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
They put you on the floor without a sound, finish reading, and go out the way they came in, empty handed.

They were not the collection. They came ahead of it, to check that the way was clear.

nextObjectiveId.text: Stay put. Wait for the collection.

objectives.description:
Eleven entries over four months, and beside each one a figure that is not a price.

Two days. Six days. Nine days.

It is a delay. The crate holds the thing until enough time has passed. Nobody was paying for storage. They were paying for the distance between two hands.

That is what the bond fee is buying. Four months of lawful, boring, receipted storage, so that the wait between one man and the next looks like paperwork instead of a meeting.

Because a meeting is two faces in one room, and a room can be described afterwards by anybody who was standing in it. These people do not know each other, and this building is how they keep it that way.

nextObjectiveId.text: Burn the eleven and close the route tonight.
Leave the floor exactly as I found it.

objectives.description:
Eleven crates go up on the loading floor, and the canal watch puts the fire out before it reaches the stacks. By morning the warehouse is a customs incident.

"Route closed, warehouse under review, and everyone who used it knows we found it."

She signs it off.

"It is a result, and I will take it. In six days they will be using a different bonded warehouse, and we will be looking at nothing."

nextObjectiveId.text: Route closed, and everyone knows it.

objectives.description:
You put the floor back down to the ring in the dust, and go out through the drain with the manifest copied and the original lying face down.

She reads the copy and stops at the last line.

"Six days."

She leaves a finger on it.

"They do not know we were in the building. In six days, somebody walks in and collects while we are standing in the roof."

"You could have had a case tonight. You brought me a date. Do not do that again without asking. And thank you."

nextObjectiveId.text: Six days, and nobody knows we were there.

objectives.description: Warehouse read.
The floor, the eleventh crate, and the manifest.
Four ways at it, and the night is not getting longer.

data.name: Old Ghost
data.description: An old Bingo Book entry, faded and worn, pinned to the mission board with a fresh brief. Old Ghost. Resurfaced after years in hiding. Once ran an ANBU cell in this village.
data.successDescription: Four squads have filed this report. The entry is still open.

objectives.description:
You wander into the missions hall, looking for your next job. A serious one this time, you decide.

Your eyes wander the board, sorting by rank. Then you see it.

An old Bingo Book entry, faded and worn, pinned to the board with a fresh mission brief.

Old Ghost. Resurfaced after years in hiding.

Dangerous and resourceful fugitive from justice. Old Ghost once ran an ANBU cell in this village.

Current whereabouts unknown. Slums district is a good lead.

If he really is back, time matters. Someone like that moving freely inside the walls will not stay quiet for long.

You think about where to begin.
The wall walk runs the whole northern span. If he came in, he came over something.

Nothing. Fresh mortar, a bored sentry, and a long climb for no reason.

The sentry has been on this stretch eleven days and has seen nobody but the mortar crew.

You are looking in the wrong place.
The market is loud, crowded, and full of people who would notice a stranger. You work the stalls.

Plenty of rumours and none of them the same twice. A fugitive is worth talking about whether or not you have seen one.

By midday you have four descriptions of four different men, and the last one is you.

This is a waste of daylight.
The back alleys behind the cooperage are where you would go if you wanted to move unseen. So you follow them.

Somebody is moving ahead of you and moving fast, and you take three streets and a wall to run them down.

A courier. Fourteen years old, terrified, carrying somebody's laundry.

You send him on and lean against the wall.

Time you do not have.

You decide to search the Slums. Eastern side of the village, most of it fallen into disrepair.

People live here out of necessity. A life inside the walls beats one without.

Nobody here is going to volunteer anything. You will have to choose how you work it.

Three ways to do this, and the day is already half gone.

nextObjectiveId.text: Find an old contact from your Chunin days.
Wait until dusk and watch for movement.

objectives.description:
You ask. People stop talking when you get close and start again when you pass.

One man points you at a doss house. The doss house points you at a scrap yard. The scrap yard points you back at the doss house.
You spend the afternoon walking in a circle somebody drew for you.

By dusk you have four addresses, three of them empty and the fourth a woman who has never heard the name. But the fourth one flinched.

She flinched at the name, not at you.

Whoever he saw today, he saw them here, and he has already finished.

nextObjectiveId.text: The east gate. Cut him off before he leaves.

objectives.description:
You reach the east verge as he is walking out of it. He stops, looks at how hard you are breathing, and seems almost sorry for you.

"You have been at this all day."

"I was done by noon."
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
He is over the verge and into the treeline, and you have nothing but a day of walking.

Somewhere behind you a doss house is pointing somebody at a scrap yard.
You still know people from before you made rank. One of them runs a back room off the tannery row and owes you nothing, which is why he will talk.

The room is small and he keeps his voice down the whole time.

"Old Ghost. Yes. Warehouse off the cut, tonight."

He gives you a door and does not ask why you want it.

The door is unlocked, the warehouse is empty, and two come off the rafters the moment you are three steps in.

This was never his location.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
The rafters were a good place to wait and they had been waiting a while.

You come to on an empty floor with two hours gone and a door standing open.

Two down in an empty building. Nobody here has been in the same district as Old Ghost tonight.

A setup. Not by your contact, who was told the same thing you were, but by whoever fed it to him.

Somebody wanted you in an empty warehouse for two hours.

nextObjectiveId.text: So where were they not sending me?

objectives.description: You go back to what you were told and work out what it was built to keep you away from. The cut runs north to the old dye works and the dye works have a night watchman nobody has paid in a month.

The dye works. Two hours late, but not too late.

There are lights on in a building that has no reason to have lights, and three sets of prints in the yard mud.

Two of them are not his.
He does not look surprised to see you. The other two move to put you between them, and he lets them, and only then does he step forward himself.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
Three of them in a yard, and the two were only ever there to hold you still.

By the time you are up the dye works are dark and the lights are off in a building that had no reason to have them.
You find a roofline with a view of the whole eastern quarter and you wait for the light to go.
Two hours after dusk, three figures leave a house at the bottom of the slope and move up the lane without lamps.

They are good. Spaced, quiet, and taking the route with the fewest windows on it. You follow anyway.

At the third corner the lead figure stops without turning around.

They know.
The two at the back turn to meet you and the third does not. He is already moving, and he does not look back once.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
Two of them in a narrow lane is a poor place to be, and the third is gone regardless.

The house at the bottom of the slope is empty by the time you get down to it.

Two down in the lane, and a long way up the slope somebody is still running.

He has not looked back once, which means he knew the other two were staying the moment he decided to leave them.
You go after him. Over the slope, across four roofs, down into the drainage cut and out the other side.

He runs out of village before he runs out of breath.

The cut ends at the wall and he turns to face you, and he is not even breathing hard.

"You are the fifth," he says. "Or the sixth. I have stopped counting properly."
No escort, no rafters, and nowhere left to be. He rolls his shoulder once and waits for you to come to him.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
He has been getting out of places like this since before you were born.

When you look up, the foot of the wall is empty and there is nothing to say he was ever standing at it.

Alone at the foot of the wall, with the two he left behind still in a lane on the other side of the slope.

Three down in a dye works yard. He waited for the other two to commit before he moved once, which is how he has stayed in that Bingo Book.

He is down at the verge with his business already concluded and nothing on him to show what it was.

You file it that night. Old Ghost. Bingo Book entry. Taken inside the village.

She reads it. Then reads it again.

"...Did you?"

"I believe your report. I have believed four of them."

She signs it and does not close the entry.

"He was ANBU here once. I was on the road the first time somebody confirmed him dead. Take the pay and do not think about it too hard."

nextObjectiveId.text: Ask how she was so sure it was him.

objectives.description:
She signs it without another word and does not close the entry.

When you are at the door she says it to your back.

"Many have reported the same. Myself included."

"Because he taught me how to be sure."

She does not look up from the page.

"That is all you get. The entry stays open. It always does."

nextObjectiveId.text: The entry stays open. It always does.

objectives.description:
The pay is A rank and it clears the same day.

The entry stays open.
Report filed. Entry open.
The slums, and three ways to work it.
The board, and four places to look.

data.name: Protection
data.description: A grain merchant has been paying someone every eighth day for two years. He reported it last week because the price went up. He has never been given a name. Stand three nights at his yard and make sure nobody collects.
data.successDescription: Whoever runs it never visits the yard and never meets his own men. A loose stone in a wall is the only place he has to be.

objectives.description:
A guard posting on the board. Three nights at a grain yard on the north row, starting tonight.

The slip reads: C rank. Make sure nobody collects.

A ledger column. Every eighth day, for two years, the same amount, written down as cartage costs.

The merchant reported it last week. The note says he did it because the price went up, not because he wanted to.

Nobody knows who takes the money. He has never been given a name, and he has never asked for one.

The yard is grain sacks, a weighbridge, a street front, and a back gate onto a lane.

The merchant meets you at the weighbridge and does not shake your hand.

"Back gate, after close. It is never the same man twice."

"Two years I have paid it, and I want you to understand why. It was less than a burnt yard, and there was nobody to report. You cannot hand a hall a man with no name and expect them to write anything down."

"Then the price went up, and I could put a number on it, and a number is a thing a hall will read."

"I want three quiet nights, and then I want you gone. I would like to be honest with you about that."

The yard goes quiet after the last cart, and the lane behind the gate goes quiet after that.

You can stand where the lane can see you, or you can be somewhere it cannot.
You take the gate and stand where the whole lane can see you.

Nothing comes up the lane. A man walks past the mouth of it once, does not slow down, and does not come back.

One evening the merchant closes early and does not say why.
You take the gate again and stand in it for six hours.

Nobody comes up the lane at all.

And now you understand it. Nothing is going to come up that lane while you are standing in it. Whoever keeps walking past its mouth understands it too.
You put yourself behind the sack stack with the gate in view, and you let the lane look exactly the way it looked last month.

Two come up the lane a little after midnight.

One goes to the gate. The other stops twenty feet short and stands facing back the way they came. He does not look at the gate once.

One collector. One lookout.

The one at the gate has a hand on the latch when you come off the stack. The lookout is already turning.

Neither of them runs. They have done this enough times to know that running is what gets you chased.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
Two of them at a back gate in the dark, and the yard is a bad place to be outnumbered.

The gate stands open when you get up, and the lane is empty. Inside the house a lamp goes on, and then goes off again. The merchant has decided not to come out.

In the morning he pays the hall for more nights. He does not look at you while he does it.

The collector sits against the gate post and does not pretend to be anything else. He lets you go through his coat. There is nothing in it but a folded cloth for carrying coin and a stub of wax.

He answers everything, flat. Nobody sent him. He takes the pickup and keeps a fixed cut of it. He has never met the man he leaves it for.

He works out what the answer is worth to him, and gives it anyway.

A drop. A loose stone in a wall, and he has never once seen who empties it. The man does not come to the yard, and he does not meet the men who do.

That is the whole design. A collector who has met him could describe him, and a man who can be described can be sold. A stone cannot be questioned and does not want a cut.

And if you take him in tonight, someone new is standing on this gate in eight days.

He walks in without arguing and gives a statement that is short and true.

Extortion, a name on a docket, and a merchant who gets a season of quiet out of it.

The handler logs the charge and pays out the posting.

"He cannot name anyone above him, because there is no one above him he has ever seen."

"It is a real charge, and it stops exactly here. That is where these things usually stop."

nextObjectiveId.text: A charge, and it stops there.

objectives.description:
He takes you to it, because the other choice is a cell, and he has already decided which he prefers.

Four streets away, a dead wall behind a barrel maker's yard, and a stone at knee height that comes out clean. The space behind it is dry and worn smooth.

You report it to the hall.

"No arrest. The merchant keeps paying for a few more weeks while somebody watches a wall."

"You let a collection happen. You also brought back the one thing in this that does not move."

Three nights, no collection, a full ledger.

The handler signs the posting off and pays out without comment.

On the last morning the merchant walks you to the gate and stops there.

"They will be back when you are not. I am not blaming you. I want you to know that I know it."

nextObjectiveId.text: Three quiet nights, and then gone.

objectives.description: Three nights stood.
The yard after close, and the lane behind the gate.

data.name: Nothing to Report
data.description: A warehouse clerk is carrying two years of bonded collection sheets to a village audit that sits at first light. The people who would rather those books did not arrive are trained. Safehouse to records hall, before dawn.
data.successDescription: The books went onto the audit table at first light. They name a broker, a bank and eleven dates, and not one member of the Forsworn, because the clerk has never met one.

objectives.description:
B rank. An escort. One clerk, one satchel, safehouse to records hall, before dawn.

The desk sends this one upstairs.

"Warehouse clerk. He is carrying two years of collection sheets from the bonded yard on the canal, and the audit opens at first light."

"B rank, because I expect the people who would rather those books did not arrive to be trained."

nextObjectiveId.text: Does anybody know he came to us?

objectives.description:
"Somebody does. He has not been at work in two days, and nobody from that office has asked why. An office that does not ask is an office that has been told not to."

"They do not need him dead. They need him not to arrive, and that can be bought on a road or bought at a door."

"Assume both have been bought, and assume the two were bought separately. Nothing these people do is organised from one desk. That is the only reason any of it is survivable."

The clerk is in the front room with his coat already on and the satchel in his lap.

"I am not brave. I want that written somewhere."

"I countersigned eleven of these. I would like the audit to be able to say that I stopped at eleven."

The clerk waits in the front room with his coat on and the satchel held in both hands. He does not ask where you are taking him. He is saving his questions.

Four ways out of the district, and first light is coming.
The north gate is shut at this hour, which you knew. The wall beside it is not.

You are up the wall and back down inside a minute. Then you look at a man of fifty holding a satchel with both hands.

He does not say anything. He does not have to.
You take the market row at his pace and hang back a little, listening for anyone who takes note of him.

Three lit corners and perhaps sixty people, and nobody stops you.

At the second corner, a figure sitting on a barrel looks at the clerk's face slightly too long, then looks down again, and does not move.

"That man knows me. He signs for the cartage at the yard."

He says it without stopping. Somebody is going to know which way you went, and the night gives them time to be somewhere before you are.
The lanes are shorter and unlit, and unlit lanes in this district have owners. You read the corner stone before you take the third turn.

One chalk stroke, low, and the powder at its edge is fresh.

Somebody has claimed this lane for an hour tonight. And you are about to walk a man of fifty down it.

nextObjectiveId.text: Go anyway. Better here than at the hall.

objectives.description:
They come off the wall at the halfway point, quick and light and not interested in you at all. They go past your shoulder, for the man behind you.

Not a robbery. Not a warning. Somebody was told a lane, an hour, and a face.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
You are turned around for two seconds, and the lane is empty behind you.

Two streets over you find him against a wall, with the satchel in both hands and no intention of letting go of it.

"I did not run. I want that written down as well."

nextObjectiveId.text: Back to the safehouse and start again.

objectives.description: The towpath is long and wet and empty, and there is a patrol on it that you have to wait out before you can put a civilian on the bank.

Fifty minutes gone that you did not have.

The clerk does not complain once. Somewhere behind the roofline, the sky stops being black and starts being a colour.

You are going to arrive. You are going to arrive in daylight. And anyone who wanted time to get ahead of you has had it.
You bring him up the last four streets slowly, stop him at the corner, and give the hall steps a long look.

One of them. Blank half mask, hands where you can see them, making no attempt at all to hide. They have been sitting there a long time.

The clerk makes a small sound.

nextObjectiveId.text: Tell him the truth about what happens after.
Tell him it ends when the books are on the table.

objectives.description:
You tell him the truth. Handing those books over makes him a witness. A witness is a thing with a price on it. The village will move him, and being moved is not the same as being safe.

He listens to all of it.

"Eleven."

He walks past you toward the steps, and he does not look at the wall.

nextObjectiveId.text: Then I will handle the wall.

objectives.description:
You tell him it ends when the books are on the table. That he goes home afterwards. That the wall is nothing he needs to think about.

He believes you, which is worse than if he had not.

He goes up the steps almost quickly, and the relief on his face is going to be a thing you remember.

nextObjectiveId.text: Then I will handle the wall.

objectives.description:
They stand up only when the hall door closes behind him. They were never here for the clerk. They were here for you.

Think it through and it is simple. If the one who walked him gets home untouched, the next clerk finds an escort willing too. They were paid to make sure the next clerk does not.

No talking. No offer. No attempt to leave.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
They were waiting a long time, and they are not tired.

They leave you where you fall. The beating was the message, and it has been delivered.

When you get up, the wall opposite is empty, and the clerk is inside with four hours of auditors and no idea that any of it happened.

The books go onto the audit table at first light, and the auditors have four hours with them before anyone else is awake.

A broker, a bank, eleven dates, and a delay column nobody outside the yard has ever seen.

Not one line of it names a Forsworn. It never could. The clerk has never met one. That was always the point of the crates.

She reads the auditors' first note standing up.

"That is a case. Cases against these people are thin on the ground."

Then she asks what you told him on the steps. Flatly, the way she asks things she has already guessed.

nextObjectiveId.text: I told him it ends when the books land.

objectives.description:
She nods once, and does not look relieved.

"Good. He handed them over knowing, which means the audit has a witness who understood what he was doing. That holds up in court."

"Also, he deserved to know. I would put that reason first. But on a bad night you will only have one of the two, and either will do."

She puts the note down and looks at you slightly too long.

"He will find out. Not tonight, and not from me. And he will remember that somebody stood on those steps and told him otherwise."

She does not raise her voice at any point.

"The audit stands. Next time, tell them, and let them be brave on purpose. It holds up better in court, and it holds up better afterwards."
Clerk delivered.
The safehouse, and four ways out of the district.

data.name: Chalk and Corner
data.description: Four corner stones. Each one has a chalk mark. Record what is on each stone and the hour you saw it. Do not scrub anything. Do not add anything.
data.successDescription: The chalk marks were a schedule, not a boundary.

objectives.description:
The mission desk is busy. The handler does not look up. He slides a folded paper across and keeps talking to someone else.

The slip reads: C rank. Survey. Four corner stones.

Inside are four rubbings: chalk marks pressed onto paper with the flat side of a pencil. One mark from each stone.

The job: record what is on each stone, and the hour you saw it. Do not scrub anything. Do not add anything.

Someone has added a note at the bottom in different handwriting: best guess is territory. Four marks, four owners.

nextObjectiveId.text: Four gangs would mean four fights.

objectives.description:
But nobody has been hurt on any of those four streets. Not once.

So the marks are not a war over territory. They are something else.

The stone worth watching is the one that changes.
Four corners, an hour of walking between them, and one afternoon.

nextObjectiveId.text: Walk all four and record them.

objectives.description: You spend an hour on the tannery row asking who chalks the corner stones.

Nobody chalks the corner stones. Nobody has even seen it happen. Two people ask if you are from the cartage office.

An hour spent, and you learned one thing: someone has asked this street these same questions before.
The first corner is exactly where the rubbing says. So is the second.

The third stone has two strokes instead of one. The second stroke is new, still powdery at the edge where nobody has stepped on it.

The fourth stone has one stroke, older than the rest.

Four corners, four hours, and one stone that changed today.

nextObjectiveId.text: Wait by the third stone and watch who comes.
Hand in the survey and let the office work it out.

objectives.description: You pick a doorway across from the third stone. You settle in and watch.

Someone comes. They crouch at the stone with a chalk stub and start a third stroke. They do not look around once.

They keep glancing up at the light, not at the street. They are checking the hour.

They place the new stroke beside the old one, with the same gap between.
Rag over the mouth. No plate on the forehead. They grab for the chalk first, not for you. The chalk matters more to them than the fight.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
They wipe out the half-made stroke with a sleeve and go over the wall before you are on your feet.

By the time you are up, the lane is empty again. Somewhere out of sight, a stroke is going onto another stone.

You hand in the four rubbings, the four hours, and what you saw in the alley.

The handler reads your notes once in the order you walked them. Then again in the order the strokes were made. Then he looks up.

"These are not property marks. Each stroke is an hour. The stones are a schedule. Someone is telling someone else when a lane will be empty."

"Not four owners. A queue."

"These crews do not know each other, and they do not want to. Two of them working the same lane on the same night is how people get seen. But you cannot sort that out in a room, because a room means faces, and a face is the one thing none of them will give up."

"So they sort it out on a wall. Nobody meets anybody, and everybody knows whose hour it is."

You hand in the four rubbings and the four hours. That is the job, all of it.

The handler checks them off, pays out, and drops them in a tray with forty other surveys.

Someone will read them properly in a month.

nextObjectiveId.text: That is the job, all of it.
